movesets.name: Trick Room Attacker
movesets.description:
• Diancie is a premier Trick Room attacker due to its fantastic bulk that allows it to set Trick Room for itself repeatedly. It also allows Diancie to snowball out of control while stacking Defense boosts from Diamond Storm, which hits a majority of the metagame for at least neutral damage and makes Diancie extremely difficult to remove with physical attacks.

  • Diancie's ability, Clear Body, provides crucial immunity to Intimidate that would otherwise be a nuisance to Diancie's damage output throughout the game.

  • Defense boosts from the aforementioned Diamond Storm create a threatening combination with Body Press, allowing Diancie to deal strong single target damage that the majority of the metagame does not resist and trade damage with opposing Trick Room attackers like Iron Hands.

  • Diancie runs Hard Stone to further boost the spread damage of STAB Diamond Storm. Hard Stone also allows Diancie to make consistent progress into one of its biggest checks, Landorus. Hard Stone can often be replaced with Covert Cloak to assist with its capability to set and make the most of Trick Room. It is used to block Fake Out, which would otherwise inhibit Diancie's ability to position itself to fire off attacks or set Trick Room. Conversely, Leftovers are used to increase Diancie's longevity and make use of its immense natural bulk.

  • Diancie has two premier Tera types. Tera Dragon is the most common and used to resist Water- and Grass-type attacks while being better into Landorus Sludge Bomb. Another thing to consider with Tera Dragon is the lack of threatening Fairy-type attacks in the metagame to punish it. Tera Grass is used to let Diancie resist Ground-, Grass-, and Water-type attacks, as well as improving its matchup into Amoonguss, which moves before Diancie in Trick Room.

  • Minimum Speed investment with 0 Speed IVs is optimal on most Diancie sets due to its threatening presence in Trick Room; once the dimensions have been twisted, it moves before threats like Ursaluna-B.

  • Common checks to Diancie include Gholdengo and Landorus because of their consistent ability to OHKO Diancie. Gholdengo is especially threatening to Diancie because it is immune to Body Press and resists Diamond Storm while threatening a OHKO back. Ogerpon formes deal threatening Grass-type damage, and Ogerpon-W in particular has a super effective Ivy Cudgel. The Ursaluna formes are also threatening for Diancie, threatening OHKOes before Diancie has Terastallized and Speed tying Diancie in Trick Room, making them troublesome for it to defeat. Okidogi can also prove difficult for Diancie, as it resists both its attacking moves and threatens large damage in return.

  • Good teammates for Diancie include Pokemon that can threaten its checks, which include Gholdengo and Iron Hands. Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W are often paired with Diancie due to Follow Me redirection, and their strong STAB combinations complement Diancie. Ogerpon-H is often paired with Diancie to threaten Gholdengo, and Ogerpon-W threatens Landorus.

  • Roaring Moon and Landorus are strong additions to Diancie cores to provide a faster mode and threaten aforementioned threats to Diancie like Okidogi and Gholdengo. Trick Room attackers like Ursaluna and Torkoal that take advantage of Diancie's ability to set Trick Room and healing partners like Sinistcha and Amoonguss that increase Diancie's longevity are also greatly appreciated.

  • Fake Out support from Pokemon like Rillaboom and Incineroar is appreciated by Diancie, allowing it to use Trick Room more easily. The latter is able to enhance Diancie's natural bulk due to its Intimidate.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 8-10 points

Overview: Diancie's stat spread lends it to being primarily a defensive Pokemon, boasting high defenses alongside a typing that grants it some key resistances. This combos well with its support movepool, allowing it to assume a plethora of roles. However, it also has decent attacking stats, granting it the ability to be offensive, using its great STAB moves, useful coverage, and range of setup moves to enable itself. On the flip side, Diancie has several shortcomings, such as its typing having several common weaknesses, with Steel-types in particular being extremely dangerous for it. In addition, it has low HP and Speed stats, both of which can potentially compromise its offensive and defensive capabilities.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Entry Hazard Setter: Diancie gets access to both Stealth Rock and Spikes, meaning it can attempt to stack as many hazards as possible. This set aims to either stack hazards at the start of a game to immediately pressure the opposing team or use its numerous switch in opportunities to set hazards gradually over the course of a game.

Bulky Support: Dipping into its support movepool, Diancie has numerous ways to enable its teammates, such as Baton Pass, Encore, and dual screens. By maxing out its bulk, it can hit the field multiple times to continue to support throughout the match.

Setup Sweeper: Diancie has access to numerous setup moves. Rock Polish and Trick Room offer speed control, Calm Mind boosts Diancie's offense to more threatening levels, and Iron Defense and Diamond Storm pair well with Body Press to create a defensive and offensive threat. Since its offenses are not world-breaking, it needs support to weaken the opposing team if it intends to attempt a sweep.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Diamond Storm, Power Gem, Meteor Beam, Moonblast, Draining Kiss, Play Rough

Setup Moves: Rock Polish, Calm Mind, Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Spikes, Encore, Light Screen, Reflect, Baton Pass, Trick Room, Rock Tomb, Bulldoze

Coverage: Earth Power, Flash Cannon, Psyshock, Psychic, Body Press, Gyro Ball, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Scorching Sands: Scorching Sands is an alternate option to Earth Power that is slightly weaker but allows Diancie to potentially spread burn. This should be used solely on support sets, as offensive sets need as much power available as possible.

Stored Power: Some sets focus on Diancie attempting to acquire as many stat boosts as possible. This strategy pairs perfectly with Stored Power, making it ridiculously strong under these conditions.

Endeavor: Diancie's defensive stat spread often means it will be knocked down to low HP, powering up Endeavor and allowing it to bypass its normally lackluster offenses to deal massive damage to the foe. When paired with Endure, Diancie can potentially knock down foes to just 1 HP.

Common Items

Leftovers: Diancie has no reliable recovery outside of Rest and Draining Kiss, meaning Leftovers is an invaluable item for it. This can be paired with Protect to extract as much use out of Leftovers as possible.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Being vulnerable to all entry hazards, Diancie can find itself worn down easily. Heavy-Duty Boots sacrifices passive recovery to allow Diancie to switch in and out more frequently throughout a game, as well as avoid the potentially game-ending Toxic Spikes.

Sitrus Berry: In situations where Diancie will be taking big hits, Sitrus Berry can provide a burst of health recovery, putting its health above the threshold needed for the foe to KO it and granting Diancie more turns on the field.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Diancie has a few weaknesses to common types, allowing foes to easily slot in coverage moves to break it down. Resistance Berries such as Babiri and Shuca Berry can allow Diancie to survive a potential KO from these attacks.

Air Balloon: Ground-type moves are common in the format, and being weak to them means Diancie appreciates the support of an Air Balloon, providing it a potential free switch against said moves with the added benefit of avoiding Spikes and Toxic Spikes.

Light Clay: Used solely on sets that focus on setting dual screens, Light Clay will extend the duration of these moves, granting its teammates more time to take advantage of them.

Power Herb: This should be used on sets using Meteor Beam, allowing Diancie to bypass its charging turn.

Custap Berry: In a similar vein to Endeavor, Diancie being knocked down to low health can enable Custap Berry, allowing it to bypass its low Speed to fire off an attack or support move in a pinch. This can also be paired with Endure to ensure it activates safely.

Tera

Although Diancie shouldn't be considered for your main Tera Captain, it makes for an excellent backup Tera Captain. Diancie will primarily be using Tera to allow itself to set up more easily using one or more of its many setup moves, using Tera types such as Tera Fairy, Water, and Steel for this purpose. Also, offensive sets can also take advantage of powerful coverage options provided by Tera, with Tera types such as Tera Fire and Ground able to grant Diancie options to bypass Steel-types. Finally, Tera Fighting can give Diancie STAB on Body Press, making it a perfect candidate for an Iron Defense set.

Draft Strategy

Diancie is not a Pokemon you center a draft around. Instead, it should be drafted with the aim of supporting other Pokemon with its vast array of utility moves, whether that be with entry hazards, dual screens, or something else. There are many different Pokemon that work in tandem with Diancie's support, which can also work to support it in the process.

Wallbreakers / Cleaners: Thanks to the numerous entry hazards Diancie can set up, it is able to support dangerous wallbreakers and cleaners that have their switch-ins constantly chipped down throughout the game. Additionally, Diancie can also be a slow pivot thanks to its low Speed and access to Baton Pass, allowing it to bring teammates in safely. Wallbreakers such as Palafin and frail cleaners such as Iron Valiant and Weavile benefit greatly from this kind of support.

Setup Sweepers: Diancie can provide multiple opportunities for teammates to safely switch in and start setting up, whether it's by using Encore or setting up dual screens. This can allow it to create potential endgame scenarios when paired with the right teammates. Setup sweepers such as Baxcalibur, Dragonite, and Volcarona become extremely dangerous when given free turns thanks to Diancie.

Steel-type Answers: Steel-types are the absolute best answer to Diancie, and as such, it benefits from teammates that can KO Steel-types for it as well as sponge their attacks. Fire-types such as Cinderace and Skeledirge and Ground-types such as Garchomp are able to take on Steel-types offensively and threaten them with powerful super effective STAB attacks, reducing the number of threats Diancie has to deal with.

Naturally Faster Teammates: Diancie is naturally slow, and thus it is reliant on a turn to set up if running some form of speed control such as Rock Polish. A way to offset this reliance is to pair Diancie with naturally faster teammates that can take over for it in a pinch. Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Greninja, and Cinderace are examples of naturally fast Pokemon that can work in this role.

Checks and Counters

Steel-type Pokemon and Coverage: Diancie suffers from a nasty 4x weakness to Steel, meaning not only do Steel-types themselves have a major advantage over it, but many Pokemon can run Steel-type coverage moves to lure it and score a surprise KO. Scizor and Metagross are prime examples of bulky Steel-types that can take Diancie's attacks and threaten it with Bullet Punch in return. Additionally, Pokemon that Diancie may usually check such as Urshifu-S can run moves like Iron Head to lure Diancie and render it useless.

Residual Damage: Lacking reliable recovery means Diancie is prone to being worn down throughout a game, notably through passive damage, and it cannot run every item it wants to try and compensate for this. Simply switching into attacks all game will rack up damage, especially if lacking Leftovers, leaving Diancie prone to being KOed more easily the longer a game goes on.

Bulky Walls: Although Diancie has some nice offensive traits, it lacks initial power to break through some bulkier Pokemon. As such, Pokemon that can take Diancie's attacks and wall it make for good counters that can wear it down and take advantage of its lack of reliable recovery. Bulky Pokemon such as Skarmory, Gholdengo, and Vaporeon can sponge Diancie's attacks, heal themselves, and threaten Diancie with their attacks in return.

Entry Hazard Removers: While simply removing hazards doesn't hurt Diancie directly, it is worth noting that Diancie has a poor matchup against most spinners, many of which are Ground-, Water- and Grass-types with STAB attacks that threaten Diancie with super effective damage and thus allow them to more easily keep hazards off the field. These include Iron Treads, Forretress, and Excadrill, which also boast a Steel typing that greatly threatens Diancie.

movesets.name: Weakness Policy
movesets.description:
• Diancie's typing and access to Encore let it find a niche in the 1v1 metagame as a bulky attacker that matches up well against several of the tier's Fighting- and Dark-type Pokemon, such as Iron Valiant and Hoopa-U.
  • Diamond Storm hits Pokemon like Volcarona and Kyurem.
  • Both Play Rough and Moonblast can threaten Dragon- and Dark-type Pokemon like Haxorus, Raging Bolt, and Hoopa-U, with the former threatening Hoopa-U a lot more and the latter being more helpful against Raging Bolt.
  • Trick Room is incredibly useful for Diancie, as it enables the use of a fast Encore after the first turn of the battle, which locks several stall and setup Pokemon, like Alolan Ninetales and Espathra, into using only one of their moves.
  • The Special Defense EVs are enough to let Diancie survive two Thunderbolts from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt, while the Attack EVs allow it to OHKO most Hoopa-U with Play Rough. Finally, the Defense EVs allow Diancie to survive two Choice Band Spirit Breaks from Jolly Iron Valiant.
  • Diancie can also run an EV spread of 252 HP / 16 Atk / 240 Def with a Relaxed nature, which gives it the best odds to survive a Choice Band Flower Trick from Adamant Meowscarada. It is better to run Moonblast on this variant as it grants Diancie better odds against Raging Bolt.
  • Since Diancie tends to struggle with Steel- and Grass-type Pokemon like Iron Crown and Ogerpon-W, Fire-type teammates like Volcanion can be useful.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
• Moonblast defeats a wide range of threats like Hoopa-U, Raging Bolt, and Choice item Iron Valiant.
  • Power Gem allows Diancie to beat non-stall Zapdos variants and Volcarona even after it has boosted once with Quiver Dance.
  • Earth Power should be used against Iron Moth and Heatran.
  • Psychic lets Diancie defeat Air Balloon Pecharunt and guarantees an OHKO against Normal Gem Sneasler. Alternatively, Flash Cannon can be used against opposing Diancie.
  • The EV spread allows Diancie to tank two Thunderbolts from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt.
  • Diancie struggles against Steel-type foes like Metagross, Iron Crown, and Hisuian Goodra; therefore, teammates like Volcarona, Ursaluna, and Volcanion are appreciated.
  • Diancie also struggles against Encore + Disable variations of Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant, so it's mandatory to have a teammate that can handle both of them, such as Volcarona and Iron Crown.

movesets.name: Wallbreaker
movesets.description:
Mega Diancie is a very potent wallbreaker that applies a lot of offensive pressure to bulky offense and balance builds, threatening Pokemon such as Zapdos, Raging Bolt, and Great Tusk. Mega Diancie’s coverage further cements its role as a wallbreaker; for example, Earth Power hits foes such as Heatran, Gholdengo, Melmetal, and Toxapex that would otherwise come in safely on its STAB moves. Mystical Fire provides even more coverage, hitting foes such as Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor. Power Gem avoids the drawback of possibly forcing Mega Diancie to run a nature that decreases Defense or Special Defense, improving its ability to take on Pokemon such as Raging Bolt. Mega Diancie does well versus common forms of entry hazard removal such as Terapagos lacking Earth Power, Great Tusk, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T. Mega Diancie is a unique hazard setter that can set up hazards while denying common opposing hazard setters in Heatran and Mega Tyranitar. 28 Attack EVs allow Mega Diancie to 2HKO Galarian Slowking with Diamond Storm.

Mega Diancie fits on bulky offense teams and pairs well with Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Ferrothorn, and Landorus-T that appreciate it due to its ability to threaten and force out Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, Zapdos, and Hisuian Samurott with its STAB attacks. In return, Great Tusk and Landorus-T check threats such as Mega Lopunny, Iron Head Kingambit, and Assault Vest Melmetal, which threaten Mega Diancie directly. Landorus-T also brings Mega Diancie in safely with a U-turn against Pokemon that like to come in on it such as Tornadus-T, Mega Charizard Y, and Great Tusk, which Mega Diancie punishes. Mega Diancie tends to struggle with fast offensive Water-types such as Ogerpon-W, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Mega Swampert in the rain. Thus, Pokemon such as Dragonite, Raging Bolt, and Ferrothorn can keep these foes in check.

movesets.name: Lead
movesets.description:
Mega Diancie functions as an amazing hyper offense lead, being able to set up Stealth Rock behind Substitute while also denying opposing entry hazards via Magic Bounce. Mega Diancie's main niche over other hazard setters is its ability to deny hazards from Pokemon such as Glimmora and Landorus-T, as well as blocking Taunt and Encore from Pokemon like Tornadus-T and Iron Valiant, making it harder for them to deny hazards. Endeavor lets Mega Diancie heavily chip Moonblast switch-ins like Moltres, Corviknight, and Heatran when at low HP. Staying in base forme is often an option in order to set Stealth Rock on faster Pokemon due to Diancie's superior bulk. 240 HP EVs allow Mega Diancie to set Substitute four times as opposed to three, leaving Mega Diancie at 1 HP to use Endeavor with.

Being a hyper offense lead, Mega Diancie's main function is to set entry hazards to enable one of the archetype's many sweepers to punch through defensive cores and win the game, often being able to give them a free switch in by wearing itself down via Substitute. Examples of Pokemon that benefit from these hazards include Kingambit, Volcarona, and Great Tusk, since they all appreciate Stealth Rock chipping down Pokemon such as Corviknight, Heatran, and Landorus-T for them to break through more easily. However, lead Mega Diancie can sometimes be threatened by super effective attacks from faster foes such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, as well as by strong priority moves from Pokemon such as Choice Band Rillaboom and Mega Scizor. These can be taken care of by partners such as Dragonite, which can safely switch in on Urshifu-R, Landorus-T, and Rillaboom, and Volcarona, which switches in on and threatens Rillaboom and Mega Scizor with its strong STAB moves.

movesets.name: Mixed Wallbreaker (Rock)
movesets.description: Mega Diancie is the ideal Mega Evolution for Rock teams due to its ability to check Dragon-types like Kommo-o, punish passive Pokemon and entry hazard setters such as Toxapex and Klefki with Magic Bounce, and be a mixed wallbreaker that threatens Great Tusk and Galarian Slowking. Diamond Storm does considerable damage to special walls like Blissey and Alolan Muk and can also provide a Defense boost. Psychic heavily damages Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Nidoking, which eases the matchup against Poison teams. Earth Power deals heavy damage to Steel-type Pokemon like Heatran and Iron Treads and is paired nicely with Mystical Fire to damage Skarmory and Corviknight. On a hyper offensive team, Mega Diancie runs four attacks for coverage. With Shuckle's Sticky Web up, its good Speed tier becomes more devastating and outspeeds Pokemon like Mega Gallade and Zeraora. Mega Diancie also pairs well with Omastar and Terrakion, as Omastar takes care of the Ground matchup with a well-timed Shell Smash, while Terrakion's access to Earthquake and Close Combat takes care of most Steel-types. On bulky offense, Mega Diancie prefers to run Spikes, as the chip damage sets up a potential late-game cleanup from more offensive Pokemon on the team like Terrakion and Nihilego. Garganacl pairs well with Spikes, as Salt Cure forces a lot of Pokemon to switch out and take additional chip damage.

movesets.name: Mixed Wallbreaker (Fairy)
movesets.description: Mega Diancie is a valuable asset to Fairy teams, featuring Magic Bounce to deflect entry hazards and status, wide coverage, and strong offensive capabilities with its high Speed. Diamond Storm often increases Mega Diancie's bulk and threatens foes like Enamorus and Mega Charizard Y. Moonblast handles threats like Mega Sableye and Latias. Earth Power can be used to counter Steel teams, OHKOing Heatran, Excadrill, and Magnezone, while dealing heavy damage to the likes of Skeledirge and Garganacl. Mystical Fire targets Steel-types that don't mind Earth Power, such as Ferrothorn, Celesteela, and Mega Scizor under Psychic Terrain. Alternatively, Mega Diancie can run Nature Power and use the various terrains set by its teammates to expand its wallbreaking abilities. Stealth Rock can be used to allow Mega Diancie to set its own hazard, but four attacks are recommended given Mega Diancie's wide coverage. Klefki provides Spikes and dual screens support which allows Mega Diancie to OHKO threats like Gholdengo, and it can also carry Thunder Wave to let Mega Diancie outspeed and take out threats like Mega Gallade and Mega Aerodactyl. Tapu Koko takes on Water-types and aids in the Steel matchup by forcing out Corviknight and Celesteela. Tapu Bulu counters Ground- and Water-types like Great Tusk and Urshifu-R, while Tapu Lele takes on Poison-types and prevents priority moves from Azumarill and Mega Scizor. Iron Valiant is a great partner for the Steel matchup, but it also benefits from Tapu Koko's Electric Terrain to outspeed and take out faster threats such as Zeraora and Greninja. All of these teammates appreciate Mega Diancie's ability to bounce hazards back to the opponent, as Fairy teams do not possess entry hazard removal.

movesets.name: Lead
movesets.description:
• Mega Diancie is a great lead for offense teams thanks to its STAB combination that threatens the main Defoggers in the metagame, which include Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal, combined with its ability Magic Bounce, which allows it to serve as an anti-lead to all other suicide leads in the tier, notably including Deoxys-S, Shuckle, Smeargle, and Glimmora.

  • Once Mega Diancie can't do much else in the field, Explosion allows it to KO itself, wear down a foe, and let an ally safely come in afterwards. Earth Power is an alternative to OHKO Glimmora and situationally hit common switch-ins in Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Necrozma-DM.

  • The given EV spread lets Mega Diancie avoid an OHKO from Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent and Choice Band Marshadow's Low Kick after Stealth Rock as well as a 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal's Dark Pulse while ensuring that it outspeeds neutral-natured foes with base 120 Speed, such as Palkia-O and Mega Salamence, on top of OHKOing specially offensive Yveltal with Moonblast.

  • Especially against non-hyper offense teams, if at Team Preview it's clear that Mega Diancie's relative lack of Speed and frail nature for the metagame may render it outsped and OHKOed, it should be kept for the mid-game, where it can come into foes such as Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O to force a switch while setting at least one entry hazard.

  • Mega Diancie has significantly higher bulk before Mega Evolving, so it may be desirable to Mega Evolve it later on to withstand an attack such as unboosted Mega Salamence's Earthquake or defensive Arceus-Ground's Judgment. In very niche scenarios where Sticky Web manages to get into its side of the field, preserving Diancie's Mega Evolution to keep Clear Body for the mid-game can help preserve Diancie's Speed. Clear Body can also be used to avoid being hindered by Glimmora's Mud Shot, but this also can let Glimmora lay entry hazards instead in the event of an incorrect prediction.

  • Faster foes such as Zacian-C, offensive Arceus-Water, and Deoxys-A can prevent Mega Diancie from doing anything by immediately OHKOing it. Allies such as Primal Groudon, Yveltal, and Necrozma-DM act as good partners to mitigate this issue by providing alternatives to play around them.

  • Mega Diancie can become setup fodder to foes such as Necrozma-DM, Primal Groudon, and Zacian-C. Ditto is a solid partner to punish setup sweepers and mitigate the potential vulnerability to them.

movesets.name: Wallbreaker
movesets.description:
• Mega Diancie's unique typing allows it to be a powerful mixed wallbreaker in the tier, since its coverage is quite difficult to pivot around for standard defensive structures, which include Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Arceus-Dark, Yveltal, and Giratina-O. Mega Diancie typing also has niche defensive utility, allowing it to soft-check Yveltal, Rayquaza, and unboosted Mega Salamence. Its ability in Magic Bounce plays a vital role against hyper offense structures barring Trick Room, since being able to deny entry hazard leads such as Deoxys-S, Smeargle, and Shuckle, effectively anti-leading them, is great for defensive partners such as Primal Groudon and support Arceus formes that cannot hold Heavy-Duty Boots. Mega Diancie is also fantastic against stall because of this ability, since it counters Giratina and non-Sludge Bomb Eternatus. This role compression makes Mega Diancie a fantastic tool for bulky offense teams that need a Pokemon that does well against all playstyles in the tier if positioned correctly.

  • Earth Power is necessary to hit Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C super effectively, allowing Mega Diancie to punish them for recklessly switching in.

  • Substitute enables Mega Diancie to ease prediction against potential switches, as well as giving Mega Diancie the chance to wallbreak further thanks to the Substitute protecting it from faster threats such as Arceus-Ground and Zacian-C. Substitute also lets Mega Diancie block Nuzzle from Smeargle, effectively walling it while denying Sticky Web. Alternatively, since Mega Diancie is able to beat all the common Defoggers in the tier, including Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal, it makes for a powerful Stealth Rock user, as it is able to make progress against a predicted switch from Arceus-Dark or Rayquaza. Spikes is also a viable option, but Mega Diancie's poor longevity means it cannot stack multiple Spike layers throughout a game consistently, even if the second layer aids greatly in wallbreaking similarly to Stealth Rock.

  • The default EV spread allows Mega Diancie's Diamond Storm to 2HKO Lunala after Stealth Rock, and OHKO Rayquaza. Mega Diancie's SpA EVs enable Moonblast to OHKO defensive Zygarde after a layer of Spikes, and to 2HKO Dondozo, with Earth Power also 2HKOing defensive Primal Groudon. The defensive investment avoids a 2HKO from Chi-Yu's Flamethrower after Stealth Rock, and from offensive Ho-Oh's Brave Bird, all while also outspeeding neutral-natured base-120 Speed Pokemon such as Arceus, Mega Salamence, and Palkia-O. The alternate spread enables Mega Diancie to also avoid an OHKO from Pheromosa's Triple Axel, but it shouldn't be used alongside Substitute as it has an even amount of HP, which hinders the usage of such move.

  • Mega Evolving Diancie should be done as soon as possible to make the most out of Magic Bounce, which is needed to bounce back status conditions from Giratina-O, Alomomola, and Eternatus, as well as deny entry hazards from Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon, even if the latter is quite risky due to Mega Diancie's poor bulk. It should be noted that Mega Diancie can induce mind games against Mud Shot Glimmora when anti-leading it, since Clear Body pre-Mega Evolution protects Diancie from Mud Shot's Speed drop, meaning Mega Diancie can decide not to Mega Evolve to more easily 2HKO Glimmora and deny it from setting up entry hazards. This process is quite risky to pull off though, since it is effectively a coinflip as to whether Glimmora uses Stealth Rock or Mud Shot.

  • Although Mega Diancie can easily switch Ho-Oh and remove it via Diamond Storm, it should be careful around Ho-Oh, since Sacred Fire possibly burning Mega Diancie is a massive hinderance to its wallbreaking capabilities, especially against stall teams, where Pressure from Giratina and Eternatus quickly drains Diamond Storm's limited PP. Diamond Storm should not be recklessly spammed, as its needed to actually break through these cores in stall and bulky balance teams.

  • Mega Diancie struggles against Primal Groudon, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Primal Kyogre, since they are all able to withstand its attacks and OHKO it back with ease, or in Zacian-C's case, it can outspeed and set up on it first. On the bulky offense teams Mega Diancie fits well on, a defensive backbone is essential to control these threats. Zygarde is able to control Primal Groudon with ease; Tera Water sets can also contain Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM for Mega Diancie, while Tera Fairy variants shut down Dragon Dance Zygarde, which is able to use Mega Diancie as setup fodder thanks to Tera Ground removing its Moonblast weakness. Yveltal can either utilize Choice Scarf to revenge kill Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and boosted Zacian-C for Mega Diancie, or it can use its Life Orb set with Sucker Punch to revenge kill Ultra Necrozma and Deoxys-A for Mega Diancie; Yveltal and Mega Diancie additionally form a potent wallbreaking duo for the team. Finally, defensive Primal Groudon can form a strong entry hazard-stacking core with Mega Diancie, while Mega Diancie beats Giratina-O for it. Offensive Primal Groudon sets appreciate Mega Diancie setting entry hazards for it to more easily wallbreak. Both Primal Groudon sets are able to handle Zacian-C and Primal Kyogre for Mega Diancie.

  • Choice Scarf Yveltal is an especially good teammate, since it can pivot into Mega Diancie via U-turn, which is an important need for Mega Diancie due to its poor bulk. Yveltal can pivot Diancie in against bulkier foes such as Coil Zygarde and defensive Ho-Oh that switch in place of Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Another pivoting teammate includes Landorus-T, which checks Zacian-C and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground for Mega Diancie while letting Mega Diancie run Substitute or Spikes, as Landorus-T commonly runs Stealth Rock. Life Orb Yveltal and other offensive teammates such as Choice Band Marshadow and Meteor Beam Eternatus appreciate Mega Diancie setting entry hazards for them to break through defensive cores more easily, with the latter two Pokemon also appreciating Mega Diancie pressuring stall teams early on for them to clean up afterwards.

movesets.name: Trick Room Setter
movesets.description:
• The given EV spread allows Diancie to survive Steam Eruption from Volcanion and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-Wellspring.
  • The alternative EV spread allows Diancie to outspeed Tornadus and the Ogerpon formes in Tailwind.
